title: Have to, or get to
header_line: My analysis of one book on habits. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Do you say I have to, or I get to?

A student said: procrastination can come from associating stress with productivity, as in a parent who comes home and complains about work. The student said he read this in an NLP book, and it needs a person to check the source.

I said that parents can accidentally anchor negative things: I can not wait for the weekend, I hate my boss. I said that if you do not interpret what happens to you, you become a victim of circumstance.

A student said: I am being conscious of the little negative language I use, such as God, I have to work out today. The small comments compound. Flipping them to positive forces me to reframe the situation.

I said the word equanimity means the ability to maintain an evenness of temperament in good or bad situations, and that we can learn to elevate emotion in a positive way. Without regulating, we let boredom run into a negative spiral.
Another student said: I block time on my calendar to focus on a task I do not look forward to, so it is out of my head and I can get back to what I like.

A student said: instead of I have to drive my kids to practice, say I get to. Before you know it they will be out of the house. Thinking of the people who cannot get out of bed makes exercising a privilege.
Another said: you do not have control of the external, but you have control of how you view it. Another repeated the idea that a small share of life is what happens, and the rest is how you react.
Which of your have-tos could be a get-to?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write three things you say you have to do.
Write a task you will block time for.
Write the last time you were a victim of circumstance.
Write how you interpret it now.

check.q: What did I say equanimity is?
What did a student say about little negative comments?
What did a student say instead of I have to?

recap: Say get to. Block time. Regulate the swing.
